title: Who Is Claude Trying to Kid? - Nautilus
gist: Dariusz Jemielniak argues that Anthropic's August 2026 move to embed imperceptible watermarks and signed provenance metadata in Claude output, driven by the EU AI Act's transparency code, is an admission that humans can no longer distinguish human from machine text — leaving imperfections as the only trusted proof of a human hand.

insights.claim: In August 2026 Anthropic announced that its newly released Claude models would weave an imperceptible watermark into generated text and attach signed provenance metadata to supported file types worldwide.
insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: Provenance-by-default from a major AI lab sets a de facto industry standard and creates demand for detection and content-authentication tooling.
insights.quote: would weave an imperceptible watermark into generated text and attach signed provenance metadata to supported file types worldwide
insights.locator: In August 2026, Anthropic, the AI giant

insights.claim: The official reason for Claude's watermarking is that the European Union AI Act's transparency code demands it, and Anthropic is applying it worldwide.
insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: EU regulation is exporting compliance features globally (Brussels effect) — watch other AI labs follow.
insights.locator: In August 2026, Anthropic, the AI giant

insights.claim: Watermarking means AI output arrives pre-confessed, with consequences such as AI-written student term papers becoming detectable.
insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: Shifts usage economics for students and content mills; may push some users to non-watermarked models.
insights.quote: Somewhere, a million term papers quietly began to glow.
insights.locator: In August 2026, Anthropic, the AI giant

insights.claim: Jemielniak argues Asimov's three laws of robotics need a fourth law — a robot must not deceive humans by impersonating a human — and watermarking goes further by requiring a signature even when a human supervised and curated AI-generated text.
insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: Frames AI disclosure as an ethical baseline likely to harden into regulation.

insights.so_what: Undermines value of stylistic AI-detectors; cryptographic provenance becomes the trust layer.

insights.claim: The only proof of a human hand still trustworthy, Jemielniak argues, is the wrong note — a typo, statistical anomaly or hesitation — making imperfection a marker of authenticity.
insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: Implies a premium on verifiably human content and a market for human-authenticity signals.

insights.speaker: Dariusz Jemielniak
insights.so_what: Signals skepticism that compliance-driven transparency resolves public trust issues around AI.
